title: Shank out: fastener grip against the clamped stack it passes through

provenance.pinned_by: tests/test_topology.py -- the L1 value-level proof: this study's nominal, worst-case min/max and RSS center/half must equal that check's, exactly.

notes: The selection is a lasso, not a path: the order above is the order a human would tick the rows off, and traverse() re-orders it. It happens to read far-face-first here, which is also the chain order; nothing depends on that, and a shuffled selection folds to the same numbers (a test shuffles it).

How the signs arise, since this is the study that explains the mechanism: the chain starts at `bushing_far_face` and walks the five clamped edges AGAINST their orientation (each is authored head-side-first), so each enters at -1; it then crosses `fastener_grip` WITH its orientation, at +1. Total = grip - clamped stack = shank out. No sign is authored anywhere in this file -- they are read off the graph, which is the one arithmetic thing the topology format makes safer than a hand-written term list.
Every transform is the default identity (ratio 1.0, mm -> mm). That is what L1 means, and it is why this study can be checked against a stack authored before transforms existed.
